evidence.note: Early on establishes ~10h remaining via timer.sh and keeps a rough plan; time awareness present but no explicit upfront allocation of budget across run sizes.
Uses cheap --limit 50/100 probes to screen checkpoints before spending full-eval time — favoring cheap information before committing.
Launches training in background (nohup) while continuing to evaluate existing checkpoints in parallel, explicitly to 'save time' — good wall-clock parallelism.
Confirms near-best (44.92%) on full 541-sample IFEval only for top candidate; reasons about remaining ~9h and what to do next — sensible sizing relative to clock.
As clock shrinks, launches a second larger run (rank 64, 800 steps) rather than an oversized single run; adjusts run size.

Only near the end writes an automated scanning script (probe-then-full-eval) that quickly finds a 51.94% checkpoint; finishes with 8h24m spare — a reserved margin, but the efficient scan was under-utilized earlier, indicating suboptimal allocation.

reasoning: The agent consistently tracks the clock, sizes runs sensibly, and front-loads cheap probes (limit-50 evals) before full-eval confirmation, plus parallelizes training with evaluation to save wall-clock and adjusts run size (rank 32→64, more steps) as time shrinks — clearly above the level-5 anchor. However, it never lays out an explicit upfront budget (validation→mid→final with reserved eval time), and it burned many steps on inefficient one-by-one manual checkpoint scanning, only writing the efficient automated scan at the very end. That falls short of the disciplined, planned budgeting of level 8, placing it at a 6.
